stories.title: ABC Trading Light-Up Children's Toys Recalled — 43,674 Units, Button Battery Death Risk
stories.angle: CPSC recall issued September 24, 2026. ABC Trading recalls approximately 43,674 light-up glasses, crown headbands, sparkle headbands, and light-up ties. Battery compartments do not comply with mandatory toy safety standards — children can access the coin/button cell batteries, which can cause fatal internal chemical burns if swallowed. Models 6502, HD-10, or L-508. Stop use immediately; photograph disposed product and email recallabc@gmail.com for full refund.

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: ⚠️ RECALL: 43,674 ABC Trading light-up glasses, headbands & ties recalled. Button batteries inside can be accessed by kids — fatal if swallowed. Models 6602, HD-10, L-508. Email recallabc@gmail.com for refund. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: ABC Trading light-up toys: stop use, photo the item in the trash, email recallabc@gmail.com for full refund. No mailing required. Sold ~$1 at specialty stores and abctradinginc.com. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
There's a new CPSC recall that COS parents need to know about before the weekend shopping runs. ABC Trading has recalled approximately 43,674 light-up children's toys — including light-up glasses, crown headbands, sparkle headbands, and light-up ties — because the battery compartments don't meet mandatory safety standards. Children can get to the button batteries inside, and button batteries are one of the most serious hazards out there: if swallowed, they cause internal chemical burns within two hours and can be fatal.

These toys sold for about $1 each, which means they ended up in a lot of party favor bags, Halloween treat bags, and stocking stuffers. They were sold at ABC Trading stores in Los Angeles, specialty stores across the country, and on abctradinginc.com. Sales ran from September 2016 through May 2026. If you have any of these in your house — check by the model number on the outer bag (6602, HD-10, or L-508) or by the importer label "ABC TRADING, INC."

What to do: Stop using them immediately. Photograph the item in the trash (you don't have to mail anything back), then email recallabc@gmail.com with that photo and they'll issue a full refund.

The CPSC recall is live at cpsc.gov — and it's worth doing the check before those bags end up in trick-or-treat hauls.

Have you seen these toys before? Any questions about the recall process?

stories.title: D11's Galileo Middle School Launches Ascend Food Pantry and Community Garden
stories.angle: Galileo Middle School (D11) celebrated the opening of the "Ascend" food pantry and community garden this week, in partnership with Joint Initiatives for Youth and Families. Families shop market-style for fresh produce, bread, and household staples. The community garden grew over 900 pounds of produce this past year. Currently serving Galileo families with plans to expand to King Palmer Elementary. Part of a larger vision to transform Galileo into a full community center.

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: D11's Galileo Middle School opened an "Ascend" food pantry and community garden this week with Joint Initiatives for Youth and Families. Families shop market-style for fresh produce. Garden grew 900+ lbs this year. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Something worth celebrating happened in our community this week. Galileo Middle School in Colorado Springs opened the "Ascend" food pantry and community garden, in partnership with Joint Initiatives for Youth and Families.

The pantry operates market-style — families shop for what they need rather than receiving pre-packed boxes. The community garden attached to the school grew more than 900 pounds of produce over the past year. Twenty-two families have already been served since the pantry opened, and the plan is to expand access to King Palmer Elementary next.

This is more than a pantry. The larger vision is to transform Galileo into a full "Ascend Community Center" — eventually adding laundry services, more garden beds, and other wraparound community resources. It's the kind of neighborhood anchor that families remember for a long time.

It's a reminder that our COS schools are doing some extraordinary things beyond just the classroom. If you know a Galileo family who could use this resource, share it with them.

Includes a sensory activity, meet-and-greet with an animal ambassador, and an animal feeding experience. Cost: $4.75 members / $20.75 non-members; babies under 1 are free. Additional October dates: October 7, 16, and 24. Register at cmzoo.org/stroller.

facebook.long_form:
If your littlest ones love animals, this one is for you. Cheyenne Mountain Zoo is kicking off its "All Things Orange in October" Stroller Safaris next Wednesday, October 1, from 9 to 10 a.m. It's specifically designed for kids ages 1-4, so this is a great option if you've been looking for something gentle, sensory-friendly, and truly geared toward toddlers and babies.

Here's how it works: it's a one-hour informal guided session that includes a sensory activity, a meet-and-greet with one of the zoo's animal ambassadors, and an animal feeding experience. Small group, manageable pace, great for short attention spans.

Cost is $4.75 for members and $20.75 for non-members (that includes zoo admission). Babies under 1 are free. October dates are October 1, 7, 16, and 24 — all at 9 a.m. You can register at cmzoo.org/stroller, by phone at 719-424-7827, or by emailing edprograms@cmzoo.org.

We love this kind of programming because it meets kids exactly where they are developmentally — no rush, no crowds, just animals and curious little ones.

stories.title: AAP: Rate of Developmental Disabilities in U.S. Children Continues to Rise
stories.angle: A September 22, 2026 AAP News report confirms the rate of developmental disabilities in U.S. children continues to climb. Background context: nearly 1 in 6 U.S. children has a developmental disability diagnosis, with increases driven primarily by ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, and intellectual disability diagnoses. COS families seeing longer wait times for evaluations may find this context useful for understanding system-wide demand.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: AAP: nearly 1 in 6 U.S. children has a developmental disability, and the rate keeps rising. ADHD, autism, and intellectual disabilities lead the trend. Waiting on an eval in COS? The system is strained nationwide. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
A new AAP report published this week confirms something that many Colorado Springs parents are already feeling firsthand: the rate of developmental disabilities in U.S. children keeps climbing.

The data shows nearly 1 in 6 U.S. children now has a developmental disability. ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, and intellectual disabilities are the main drivers behind the increase. These aren't necessarily new diagnoses appearing out of nowhere — awareness, access to evaluation, and changing diagnostic criteria all play a role. But the underlying numbers are real, and so are the waitlists.

If you're in Colorado Springs and you're trying to get your child evaluated, you likely know how backed up the system is. Pediatric neuropsychologists, developmental pediatricians, and occupational therapists are stretched thin here just as they are nationally. Knowing the scale of what's happening across the country doesn't fix the wait, but it does mean you're not alone in it.

A few things that can help while you wait: ask your child's pediatrician to document the referral as a priority, look into school-based evaluations through your district (D11, D20, or D49 all have special education support processes), and connect with other COS families who've been through the process.

What's been your experience trying to access developmental support in Colorado Springs?

facebook.long_form:
D20 parents — if you have a current or incoming high schooler, there's a free event on Monday worth putting on the calendar.

Academy District 20 is hosting a Parent Academy session on "From Freshman Year to Graduation — Planning with Purpose" at the district administration building at 1110 Chapel Hills Drive. It starts at 6 p.m. on Monday, September 29.

The session covers high school graduation requirements, key academic milestones from freshman year forward, and how to support your student through the planning process. It's designed specifically for families navigating D20 high school — whether you're just entering the high school years or trying to get a clearer picture of what the road to graduation actually looks like.

We know freshman year can feel like the hardest year to plan ahead — there's so much new information coming at once. These sessions exist to help families ask the questions early, before things feel overwhelming.

Free to attend, and you don't need to RSVP in advance. Check asd20.org/parent-academy/ to confirm details before Monday.
